newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg Q1 global sales volume rises.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg Q1 global sales volume rises.

text.p: Kellogg Co, the largest U.S. cereal manufacturer, said Friday its global sales volume rose 10 percent in the first quarter, including the Lender's bagel business that was acquired in December 1996.
Excluding Lender's, Kellogg said its global volume was up three percent.

"We faced a difficult year-to-year comparison in the first quarter, and this was the last of four quarterly comparisons heavily influenced by the 1996 cereal price reductions in the United States," Kellogg chairman Arnold Langbo said in a statement.
"Still, our overall performance was encouraging, with particularly strong sales growth in cereal in Asia and Latin America and in convenience foods in North America," he added.

Earlier today, Kellogg reported first quarter earnings of $0.77 a share, down from year-ago earnings of $0.99 a share before a $0.03 charge. Kellogg said its earnings were consistent with earlier projections.
"Our U.S. cereal volume improved late in the quarter and is continuing to grow in April," Langbo said. "We also achieved market share improvement in both the U.S. and the United Kingdom."

He added the company is pleased with the performance of its two newest cereals in the United States, Kellogg's Honey Crunch Corn Flakes, introduced last fall, and Kellogg's Cocoa Frosted Flakes, which was rolled out beginning in March.
